title: Bovi’s ‘Guilty as Charged’ Introduces a Different Experience for Comedy Audiences
excerpt: The Guardian examines the reserved seating introduced at the Lagos finale of Bovi’s Guilty as Charged tour, placing the audience experience at the centre of the story.
imageAlt: Bovi beside Guilty as Charged branding

segments.text: The Guardian examines the reserved seating introduced at the Lagos finale of Bovi’s Guilty as Charged tour, placing the audience experience at the centre of the story.

The performance took place at the Eko Convention Centre on 11 October 2026. Guests received their seat allocations when booking online, giving them clarity about where they would sit before arriving at the venue.

The report considers how ticketing and seating can improve an event beyond the performance itself. It presents the Lagos production as a practical example for organisers thinking about the professional development of live entertainment in Nigeria.

title: From London to Canada and Back Home: Bovi’s ‘Guilty as Charged’ Underscores the Reach of Nigerian Comedy
excerpt: THISDAY follows Bovi’s Guilty as Charged tour across the United Kingdom, Canada and Nigeria, exploring how Nigerian comedy connects with audiences across borders.
imageAlt: Bovi beside his Guilty as Charged tour branding

segments.text: THISDAY follows Bovi’s Guilty as Charged tour across the United Kingdom, Canada and Nigeria, exploring how Nigerian comedy connects with audiences across borders.

The international run included a London performance at Indigo at The O2 on 5 April 2026 and sold-out dates across six Canadian cities. The tour returned to Nigeria for Benin City and Lagos, ending at the Eko Convention Centre on 11 October.

The feature links that reach to observational storytelling, familiar situations and shared cultural references. For Nigerians abroad, those references can offer a connection to experiences and expressions from home while keeping the comedy rooted in its original identity.

title: Play With Stephen to Host Masterclass and Press Conference in April in Commemoration of Autism Awareness Month
excerpt: Play With Stephen announced an April masterclass and press conference at Lakowe Resort in Lagos to mark Autism Awareness Month, bringing education and public conversation into its advocacy work.
imageAlt: Featured photograph accompanying the Play With Stephen masterclass announcement

segments.text: Play With Stephen announced an April masterclass and press conference at Lakowe Resort in Lagos to mark Autism Awareness Month, bringing education and public conversation into its advocacy work.

The announcement invited stakeholders, partners, journalists and community members to engage with advocates on autism awareness and inclusive participation in sport. The press conference was also intended to review the initiative’s impact and discuss its next tournament.

Founder Stephen Oluwatoyin Onaivi emphasised understanding, access and action. The programme aimed to move the conversation beyond recognition and encourage shared responsibility for more inclusive environments for autistic people.

title: Eniola Omoniyi on Building the Structure the Nigerian Creatives Need
excerpt: Eniola Omoniyi’s THISDAY feature explores the systems that help creative talent become a lasting career: a clear identity, consistent positioning, professional discipline and a dependable way of doing business.
imageAlt: Eniola Omoniyi, founder of Eni Brand Architect

segments.text: Eniola Omoniyi’s THISDAY feature explores the systems that help creative talent become a lasting career: a clear identity, consistent positioning, professional discipline and a dependable way of doing business.

The profile traces her thinking to experience in Kenya’s media and creative sector, where she observed how organisational structure and storytelling could support talent. That perspective informed Eni Brand Architect, which she founded in September 2024.

Drawing on her work as a broadcaster, television host, founder and brand professional, Omoniyi argues for infrastructure behind visibility. The article describes EBA’s approach to helping creatives, entrepreneurs and businesses turn ideas into structured brands through identity, strategy and storytelling.

title: Loud Urban Choir Performs at Bovi’s ‘Guilty as Charged’ Show in Lagos
excerpt: The Nation reports on Loud Urban Choir’s performance at the Lagos finale of Bovi’s 2026 Guilty as Charged world tour at the Convention Centre, Eko Hotel and Suites.
imageAlt: Loud Urban Choir performing at Bovi’s Guilty as Charged show

segments.text: The Nation reports on Loud Urban Choir’s performance at the Lagos finale of Bovi’s 2026 Guilty as Charged world tour at the Convention Centre, Eko Hotel and Suites.

The ensemble’s set included a mashup of Phyno’s Grateful and Abdsamad Abiola’s Tomorrow, combining rap influences with layered choral harmonies. The report notes the audience response and the circulation of a performance video online.

Introduced as Talentville Choir in 2019, the group later became Loud Urban Choir. Talentville Africa founder Ann Obaseki described the collaboration as a significant moment for two acts connected to the same talent organisation.

title: Play With Stephen: Seven Editions of Swing for Autism, from Accra to Lagos
excerpt: THISDAY looks back at seven editions of Play With Stephen’s Swing for Autism tournament, tracing an annual commitment that has connected golfers, corporate partners and advocates in Accra and Lagos.
imageAlt: Play With Stephen’s Swing for Autism initiative

segments.text: THISDAY looks back at seven editions of Play With Stephen’s Swing for Autism tournament, tracing an annual commitment that has connected golfers, corporate partners and advocates in Accra and Lagos.
The initiative began in 2020. Following editions in Ghana, including Achimota Golf Club in 2025, the seventh tournament took place at Lakowe Lakes & Country Estate in Lagos from 21 to 23 August 2026.

The report explains that tournament proceeds support beneficiary centres providing autism-related diagnosis, therapy and education. Founder Stephen Onaivi places the emphasis on dependable, continuing support for families, with the initiative’s work extending beyond the tournament weekend.

title: Loud Urban Choir Adds a Symphony to “Bovi: Guilty as Charged”
excerpt: The Guardian highlights Loud Urban Choir’s contribution to the Lagos finale of Bovi: Guilty as Charged, where a contemporary choral set added another dimension to the evening’s comedy.
imageAlt: Loud Urban Choir on stage at the Lagos comedy finale

segments.text: The Guardian highlights Loud Urban Choir’s contribution to the Lagos finale of Bovi: Guilty as Charged, where a contemporary choral set added another dimension to the evening’s comedy.

At the Eko Hotel Convention Centre, the ensemble combined close harmonies with modern Nigerian rhythms, drawing cheers and audience participation. The report places the performance within a busy year of appearances across music, sport and entertainment.

It also recalls the choir’s cover of The Angel (North London Forever) and performances at Lagos football watch parties. Together, these appearances illustrate the group’s range across different audiences and live-event settings.

title: Bovi: Behind the Punchlines
excerpt: The Nation looks beyond Bovi’s punchlines to the writing, observation, timing and audience awareness involved in developing a live comedy production.

segments.text: The Nation looks beyond Bovi’s punchlines to the writing, observation, timing and audience awareness involved in developing a live comedy production.

The feature considers his background across television, writing and production alongside stand-up performance. It describes how a central theme helps organise the material in Guilty as Charged, giving a show a recognisable identity while allowing it to explore different subjects.

The report follows the conclusion of the tour in Lagos on 11 October 2026, after performances in the United Kingdom, Canada and Nigeria. It places that finished performance within a wider creative process.

title: Bovi Closes World Tour with Lagos Comedy Night
excerpt: PUNCH reports on the Lagos finale of Bovi’s Guilty as Charged world tour, which combined stand-up performances with a musical contribution from Loud Urban Choir.
imageAlt: Bovi on stage during a comedy performance

segments.text: PUNCH reports on the Lagos finale of Bovi’s Guilty as Charged world tour, which combined stand-up performances with a musical contribution from Loud Urban Choir.

The show took place at the Eko Convention Centre on 11 October 2026. I Go Save, Mr Patrick, Funny Urch and other comedians joined the evening’s programme, while the choir performed popular Afrobeats songs.

The Lagos event completed a run that included London, six Canadian cities and a return to Nigeria. The coverage also places the tour within Bovi’s career across live comedy, television, writing and film production.

title: Lagos Golfers Club to Host 14th SWAGc Cancer Awareness Tournament
excerpt: Lagos Golfers Club announced its 14th Annual Year-End and Swing Against Cancer tournament for 28 November 2026 at Lakowe Lakes Golf and Country Club in Lagos.
imageAlt: Golf ball and club on a golf course

segments.text: Lagos Golfers Club announced its 14th Annual Year-End and Swing Against Cancer tournament for 28 November 2026 at Lakowe Lakes Golf and Country Club in Lagos.

The Nation reports that the programme is planned for 72 golfers, with an 8 a.m. shotgun start followed by lunch, a cancer-awareness session, prizes and awards. Fundraising supports screening, early detection and assistance for people who cannot afford treatment.

The report describes the club’s work with the St. Cyril Cancer Treatment Foundation and other cancer-care organisations. Sponsorships, partnerships and a charity raffle form part of the fundraising plans.

title: Comedy Offers Therapeutic Benefits, Says Bovi
excerpt: The Nation reports on Bovi’s view that comedy gives audiences emotional relief as well as entertainment, drawing on his reflections about laughter and live performance.
imageAlt: Bovi holding a microphone on stage

segments.text: The Nation reports on Bovi’s view that comedy gives audiences emotional relief as well as entertainment, drawing on his reflections about laughter and live performance.

The article revisits remarks from the press conference for his 2022 production Naughty by Nature and connects them with his continuing enjoyment of performing. It presents these as the comedian’s perspective on what audiences take away from a show.
The feature also considers comedy’s role in examining everyday behaviour and topical issues, including the central theme of his more recent Guilty as Charged production.

title: From an Idea to the Stage: The Making of Loud Urban Choir
excerpt: Independent traces Loud Urban Choir to Ann Obaseki’s idea of bringing Afrobeats into a choral setting, then follows the auditions and creative work that turned the concept into a performing collective.
imageAlt: Loud Urban Choir performing on stage

segments.text: Independent traces Loud Urban Choir to Ann Obaseki’s idea of bringing Afrobeats into a choral setting, then follows the auditions and creative work that turned the concept into a performing collective.

The report describes how familiar songs are separated into vocal parts and rebuilt through ensemble arrangements. Although contemporary African music was a starting point, the group’s approach remains open to different genres and audiences.

It also follows the choir’s development through original singles, live appearances and collaborations, showing how a distinctive vocal interpretation became the foundation for a broader musical identity.

title: ‘Every House Remembers’ Brings Four Nigerian Artists Together to Explore the House as Body, Object and Archive
excerpt: Independent introduces Every House Remembers, a group exhibition by Nomadic Gallery and BoConcept that explores memory, belonging and the relationships between bodies, objects and domestic space.
imageAlt: Two people standing beside an artwork at the exhibition

segments.text: Independent introduces Every House Remembers, a group exhibition by Nomadic Gallery and BoConcept that explores memory, belonging and the relationships between bodies, objects and domestic space.
The exhibition brings together Francis Agemo, Duke Asidere, Gbolahan Ayoola and Ato Arinze. Presented across the gallery and showroom in Victoria Island, Lagos, it runs from 1 to 28 November 2026.

Curator Mercy Imiegha’s framing connects the artists’ different materials and visual approaches through the idea of a house as a carrier of personal and inherited memory. The presentation places works both in the gallery and within furnished interiors.

title: Ann Obaseki Leads Discussion on African Cultural Intelligence at NAC 2026
excerpt: Ann Obaseki moderated a discussion on African cultural intelligence during The Red Room by MediaReach OMD at the 2026 National Advertising Conference in Abuja.
imageAlt: Ann Obaseki with fellow participants at The Red Room

segments.text: Ann Obaseki moderated a discussion on African cultural intelligence during The Red Room by MediaReach OMD at the 2026 National Advertising Conference in Abuja.

The Nation reports that the session brought together X3M IDEAS chief executive Steve Babaeko and Professor Uchenna Uzo of Lagos Business School. They explored how cultural identities, language, humour, traditions and everyday experiences inform relevant brand communication.

The conversation also considered artificial intelligence, digital platforms and consumer data while emphasising differences across African markets. Obaseki connected industry practice with academic perspectives on audience engagement and competitive brand strategy.
